compiled_state.title: As a project operator, I configure copy.artifact_dir with safe path validation so artifacts land where each project expects
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Description

**What**: Add a `copy.artifact_dir` key to dso-config.conf (default `copy/`), document it in CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md, and apply path validation that rejects absolute paths and `..` segments.
**Why**: Without configurable output and path validation, every project shares one fixed directory and is exposed to artifact write-out-of-tree via crafted config or epic-id.
**Scope**:
- IN: config key with documented default; sprint task dispatcher passes resolved path to gov-copy-writer; path validation rejects absolute paths and `..` segments; resolved path created lazily (mkdir -p) on first write; CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md update
- OUT: gov-copy artifact schema (separate story); gov-copy-writer agent (separate story)

## Done Definitions

- When this story is complete, setting `copy.artifact_dir = some/dir` in dso-config.conf causes the next gov-copy-writer dispatch to write its artifact under `some/dir/<epic-id>.yaml`
  ← Satisfies: sc-3
- When this story is complete, an absolute path (e.g., `/etc/copy`) for `copy.artifact_dir` is rejected with a clear error before dispatch
  ← Satisfies: sc-3
- When this story is complete, a path containing `..` (e.g., `../../etc`) is rejected with a clear error before dispatch
  ← Satisfies: sc-3
- When this story is complete, when the key is unset, artifacts land under the documented default `copy/<epic-id>.yaml`
  ← Satisfies: sc-3
- When this story is complete, CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md documents the key, default, validation rules, and override path
  ← Satisfies: sc-3
- When this story is complete, unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic

## Considerations
- [Security] Absolute-path and `..`-segment rejection applies to the configured value AND to any per-epic path derivation (e.g., copy/<epic-id>.yaml). Validate the resolved final path, not just the configured dir, to prevent a malicious epic-id from escaping the configured root.

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
